abstract: Experimental radiation patterns of antenna used for LAN radio Ethernet equipment of protocol IEEE 802.11, such as subscriber adapters including PC cabinet and access points, are presented.

articleTitle: Sensor and devices for powerful radioelectronic gauge and system checking
publicationTitle: 2005 5th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The theoretical and applied aspects of absorbing wall method were considered in the report. The thin wall waveguide heating process mathematical modeling allowed to determine the law of temperature field distribution on their surface. The new physical models of sensors on the basis of the absorbing wall was analyzed.

articleTitle: The radiating antenna array on the basis of electric field standing waves in the ionospheric plasma
publicationTitle: 2005 5th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Radiation of electromagnetic waves by a volume of ionospheric plasma with periodic standing waves of the electric field has been investigated. The electric field standing waves are generated by intersection in the ionosphere of two beams of continuous coherent radiowaves from ground-based facilities separated on the Earth surface by hundreds of kilometers. Radiation patterns (RP) of a plasma radiator, as well as the electric field strengths have been calculated in their maxima for different wavelengths and widths of radiowave initial beams. The plasma radiator is proposed to be used for probing electron density in the ionosphere and over-the-horizon ionospheric radio communication.

articleTitle: 2D tape scanner for microwave holography
publicationTitle: 2005 5th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The arrangement and operation principle of a new type 2D scanner antenna for radioholographic systems enabling 3D imaging is described. Design of such antennas and some results of their testing are presented.

articleTitle: Mutual impedance of electric dipoles
publicationTitle: 2005 5th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The system of two electric dipoles, separated by distance, that is less than a wavelength, is examined. Axes of dipoles are parallel and it is accepted, that electromagnetic mutual coupling between them exists. Described system can be considered as slowing structure for the cases of decameter or hectometer waves. Analytical formulas for the calculation of active and reactive parts of mutual impedance of dipoles are presented. Distance between dipoles and displacement of their ends in terms of wavelength are used as arguments in the proposed formulas.

articleTitle: The full-wave simulation of printed phased array
publicationTitle: 2005 5th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The phased array composed from printed radiators is considered. This antenna can be applied as radiation array in spiraphase focusing system. The printed element shape is arbitrary. The structure contains controlled elements (crystal diodes). These array electromagnetic characteristics are controlled by diodes. The mathematical model is obtained by integral equation method. Microstrip spiral radiators current distribution and input impedance are investigated. The numerical results can be used to develop antennas with optimum parameters.

articleTitle: Single-pulse antenna system for continuous mode millimeter wave auto radar
publicationTitle: 2005 5th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Antenna system for single-pulse continuous wave radar for 76-77 GHz frequency band is discussed. Structure, construction and parameters are shown.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation results of an object with nonlinear electric field characteristics excitation
publicationTitle: 2005 5th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Experimental investigation results of nonlinear loaded dipole and nonlinear spherical reflector excitation with biharmonic electromagnetic field are considered. Findings are compared with an appropriate boundary problem computation results.

articleTitle: Signal processing in antenna arrays when using "supersolution" algorithm
publicationTitle: 2005 5th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The algorithm of constructing of weight coefficients that guarantees receiving the source signal getting into the main maximum of directive pattern and suppressing other sources signals is investigated. Basing on the analytic form of the inverse covariance matrix for signals the estimations of the possible meanings of the signal/noise relation depending on the parameters of antenna system and signals (number and step of radiator displacement, receiving signals covariance degree) are found. The results of mathematical modelling of signal processing based on the algorithm are given.

articleTitle: The synthetic aperture radar in high frequency band
publicationTitle: 2005 5th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The possibilities of the synthetic aperture radar construction in high frequency (HF) band are analyzed. The fields of application of such radar are considered.

articleTitle: FDTD simulation of videopulse scattering by elliptic objects in different media
publicationTitle: 2005 5th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The results of computer simulation of videopulse scattering in inhomogeneous media containing conductive cylinder objects are presented in this work. The finite difference time domain method (FDTD) and Mur's absorbing boundary conditions of second order were used to solve the problem. The GPR images of the researched objects were built. The analysis and comparison of scattered electromagnetic fields for different sizes and locations of conductive objects were carried out.

articleTitle: About the use of the term "pyramid horn antenna"
publicationTitle: 2005 5th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Some aspects of terminological correctness of the traditional term "pyramid horn antennas" that is widely used in antenna engineering are discussed. Performed analysis allows making a conclusion that "obelisk horn antennas" is a more correct term for the description of this type of antennas. As an example, this term is applied to the design and experimental research of linearly polarized horn antennas excited by a section of the inhomogeneous waveguide.

articleTitle: Adaptive antenna for measuring electromagnetic wave polarization parameters
publicationTitle: 2005 5th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The suggested antenna system, which consists of two linearly polarized radiators and signal processing devices, can be adapted to any polarization of an electromagnetic wave. At the expense of consecutive use of signal processing channels antenna polarization parameter adjustment errors are minimal with regard to the values of the same electromagnetic wave parameters. Using characteristics of the antenna itself this method of polarization adaptation enables to determine polarization ellipse parameters of incident electromagnetic wave. Antenna can be applied to define direction of the incident wave. When measuring polarization parameters, the ability to find the direction of the wave is used to locate radiators of the antenna system in the wave input plane.

articleTitle: Reduction of measurement errors influence on the results of subsurface radiolocation probing
publicationTitle: 2005 5th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: This paper presents the results of the experimental research of the influence if the equipments and methodical errors of measurements upon the results of the deep radiolocation probing (up to 60 m) by the ringing excitation method in the technogenic zones with dense building. The technical solutions have been worked out concerning the reduction of this influence. The results of experimental research are given that confirm the efficiency of the solutions.

articleTitle: Intellectual system of detection low-sized air objects
publicationTitle: 2005 5th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The intellectual adaptive system of detection of low-sized air objects on a background radar clutter from the ground level environment based on overlapping of the power and spectral analysis with adaptation of detection parameters to statistics and to the average interference spectrum in a vicinity of an analyzed resolution cell is offered. Such a combined digital-logic analysis of a spectral pattern of a preliminary detection proves to be rather effective and, as show results of experimental studies, allows to lower a false alarm probability on one-two order. At the same time, it is significant, that the functional scheme of examined detector doesn't contain complicated digital and logic operations. In one's turn, it provides relative simplicity of the scheme realization in the low- and medium-range radars and also in the perspective radars with the digital spectral analysis of the signals.

articleTitle: Radiation transformation in time-varying medium
publicationTitle: 2005 5th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Transformation of radiation in a time-varying medium is considered and formation of the striped spectrum of waves is shown. The waves of a radiation have different initial shapes and complexities. Various laws of the medium permittivity change are investigated. Correlation between wave's complexity and its spectrum is shown.

articleTitle: Influence of small anisotropy on characteristics linear wire
publicationTitle: 2005 5th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The influence of small anisotropy of uniaxial medium on the distribution of the current and fields of the radiation in far zone of the symmetric linear antenna was investigated. Is shown, that in case of the perpendicular orientation of the antenna respectively axis of anisotropy the influence of small anisotropy on the researched characteristics on the order is more, than in case of the parallel orientation.

articleTitle: Multibeam antenna array with frequency-phase scanning
publicationTitle: 2005 5th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Fundamental relations necessary at designing planar antenna arrays with frequency-phase scanning are given. Technology of development of aperture elements is described and variants of practical realization with presented features are shown.

articleTitle: Excitation of wire structures with nonlinear characteristics of the surface impedance
publicationTitle: 2005 5th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: A procedure of the analysis of thin-wire structures with the distributed nonlinear surface impedance is considered, which is based on the use of nonlinear boundary conditions. The developed procedure is reduced to a software package working for the analysis of thin-wire structures with different parameters of the surface impedance under their excitation with all kinds of sources. The results of computation of nonlinear effects for the simplest radiators - symmetric and asymmetric dipoles with the inductive surface impedance - are given. There are analyzed also the input resistance of these radiators at different levels of their excitation. The difference in behaviour of the current distribution along scatterers with the distributed and lumped nonlinearities when exciting them with the plane wave field.

articleTitle: Unique filler for modern microwave absorbers with magnetic losses
publicationTitle: 2005 5th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: Paper presents brief review of properties and application of amorphous ferromagnetic microwire in glass insulation. Combination of magnetic and electrical properties make microwire a perspective filler for microwave absorber.

articleTitle: New smart beamforming - analysis and designs
publicationTitle: 2005 5th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: The results of investigation of a typical adaptive antenna array, a low cost method of a multi-null-steering with comparison to the conventional one, and analysis, design and investigation of the new type of scan antennas without using phase shifters for beam-scanning have been presented.

articleTitle: The Riemann-Hilbert problem method in the theory of electromagnetic wave diffraction by periodic structures
publicationTitle: 2005 5th International Conference on Antenna Theory and Techniques
abstract: A modern treatment of the Riemann-Hilbert problem method (the AMSh method) which is one of the classical methods of mathematical theory of waves diffraction by gratings is given. The AMSh method's modifications in terms of the field strengths and current's representations are considered. The results of the numerical modelling are presented.
